issues_detected.description: No top-level doi, and id 'https://cm4ai.org/' is identical to page 'https://cm4ai.org/', so the dataset identifier is the project web site. Yet the record's own citation names 'https://doi.org/10.18130/V3/HIGT4C', version_access gives latest_version_doi 'doi:10.18130/V3/HIGT4C', and every entry in resources carries a Dataverse DOI. The persistent identifier exists in the record but is not promoted to the dataset level.
issues_detected.recommendation: Set doi to 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C (or a series-level DOI) and use it, not the project site, as id.

issues_detected.description: Release version numbers in resources are non-monotonic and disagree with the Dataverse citation versions: June 2026 version '2.0' (citation 'V2'), October 2025 '2.1' ('V2'), June 2025 '2.1' ('V2'), March 2025 '1.4' with caveat 'the data citation on the same page gives V1'. Two different releases share '2.1' and the newest release carries a lower number than its predecessors. The record transcribes the page headings faithfully but does not flag the inconsistency at the series level.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record both the page-heading version and the Dataverse dataset version per release, and add a source_caveats line on version_access noting the scheme is per-release and not sequential.

issues_detected.description: collection_timeframes records the NIH award period ('start_date 2022-09-01, end_date 2026-08-31 ... NIH RePORTER records the project start') rather than when the SEC-MS, imaging and perturb-seq data were actually acquired. The record is explicit that these are RePORTER values, but the slot's meaning is the collection window, which the bundle does not give.
issues_detected.recommendation: Keep the award period with the grant and either leave collection_timeframes empty with a caveat or populate it from per-release publication dates as a lower bound.

issues_detected.description: Two of the three ethical_reviews entries are contact persons ('Ethical review contact, Vardit Ravitsky', reachable at an email address) rather than review events; no reviewing body decision, protocol number or determination is recorded. The third entry describes an ethics program (Value-Sensitive Design, Life Cycle framework). The slot's meaning is a review that was conducted.
issues_detected.recommendation: Move the contact persons to data_governance or maintainers and reserve ethical_reviews for a review determination, or state that no IRB determination was required (consistent with involves_human_subjects: false).

issues_detected.description: external_resources mixes URLs with bare repository names and accession identifiers: 'MassIVE Repository', 'Figshare', 'NCBI BioProject', 'MSV000097168', 'PXD052362', 'https://ndexbio.org' (organisation home, not the uuid-specific record). The MassIVE and ProteomeXchange accessions are well-formed but not resolvable as written.
issues_detected.recommendation: Express accessions as resolvable URLs (e.g. https://massive.ucsd.edu/... MSV000097168, https://proteomecentral.proteomexchange.org/... PXD052362, https://www.ndexbio.org/viewer/networks/f693137a-...).

issues_detected.description: description states 'quarterly data releases' and updates says 'frequency: quarterly', but the recorded distribution_dates are 2025-03-03, 2025-07-01, 2025-10-31 and 2026-06-17, an eight-month gap before the latest release. The claim is the project's stated cadence, not the observed one.
issues_detected.recommendation: Qualify the cadence as the stated schedule and note the observed intervals.

issues_detected.description: description reports 'a data volume of 21.4 TB' for the project, but the enumerated June 2026 release files total roughly 12.6 GB (three image archives of 3.8, 4.6 and 4.2 GB plus kilobyte-scale archives). The project-wide counter and the release inventory measure different things, and no total_size_bytes is recorded for the release itself.
issues_detected.recommendation: Record total_size_bytes for the current release from the stated file sizes and label the 21.4 TB figure as project-wide.

issues_detected.description: Instance count for 'Proteins imaged in MDA-MB-468' is 464, while notes gives 523 for the TNBC flagship grouping and the March 2025 release gave 563; the record surfaces all three in source_caveats and chooses the higher-ranked source, which is correct handling, but the 'Immunofluorescent images' count of 53788 is a project-wide web counter with no per-release breakdown.
issues_detected.recommendation: State the release each count applies to alongside the count.

issues_detected.description: distribution_formats and file_collections describe every data file only as 'ZIP' / 'application/zip'; the payload formats inside (image format for immunofluorescence, mass-spectrometry result tables, perturb-seq matrices, FASTQ/SRA) are not stated, so a consumer cannot judge interoperability of the data itself from the record.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add the contained file formats per archive (e.g. PNG/TIFF images, TSV/CSV tables, h5ad, FASTQ) from the RO-Crate metadata.

issues_detected.description: known_biases contains a single representation_bias entry. known_limitations separately records 'Incomplete overlap between data streams' and the selection of '100 chromatin regulators' is stated in collection_mechanisms; these are selection-type biases affecting any model trained on the maps but are not categorised as biases, and future_use_impacts is absent.
issues_detected.recommendation: Add selection_bias entries for the curated protein panel and incomplete modality overlap, and a future_use_impacts entry covering dual-use and commercialisation supervision that data_governance already mentions.

semantic_insights: DOI prefix 10.18130 is the University of Virginia LibraData registrant, consistent with publisher 'ROR:0153tk833' (University of Virginia) and with every access URL under dataverse.lib.virginia.edu.

Grant numbers '1OT2OD032742-01' and '5U54HG012513-02' follow the full NIH application-number format; the record documents the three renderings of the Bridge2AI award ('1OT2OD032742-01', '3OT2OD032742-01S2', 'OT2 OD032742') rather than silently choosing one.
Cell line RRIDs 'RRID:CVCL_0419' (MDA-MB-468) and 'RRID:CVCL_B5P3' (KOLF2.1J) follow the Cellosaurus RRID pattern.

Human-subjects logic is internally consistent: involves_human_subjects: false, direct_collection.is_direct: false ('The data were not collected from individuals'), is_deidentified 'De-identified Samples: Yes', confidentiality_level 'unrestricted', and 'All release files are marked Public with no access request required'.

License logic is consistent: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 is echoed in license, license_and_use_terms.data_use_permission 'no_commercial_use', prohibited_uses ('Commercial use without a separate license') and ip_restrictions naming the copyright holders; the record also correctly notes the captured license page is the deed and 'has no legal value'.
file_collections arithmetic checks out: file_count 2+3+2+2+1 = 10 equals top-level total_file_count 10 and the June 2026 resource's total_file_count 10; every file carries an md5.

Referent discipline is explicit: the U2OS Nature paper is kept out of composition, collection and funding slots ('its counts, protocols and separate funders are not carried into this record's own composition'), and the GPT-4 naming step is not asserted as a tool because the bundle names it only for the U2OS map.

Temporal ordering is plausible: project start 2022-09-01, releases 2025-03-03 through 2026-06-17, image archives republished 15 July 2026 matching last_updated_on 2026-07-15, project end 2026-08-31/November 2026 with the disagreement recorded.

No cleaning, QC, imputation or missing-data handling is documented, and the preprocessing described produces cell maps that the releases do not yet contain, so the processing actually applied to the released input streams is thinner than it appears.

questions.score_label: Single typed bias, no fairness analysis or AIO mapping
questions.evidence: known_biases (1): 'Cell line derivation limits population representation', bias_type 'representation_bias', 'derived from commercially available de-identified human cell lines and do not represent all biological variants which may be seen in the population at large', affected_subsets 'All released data streams'. future_use_impacts absent. known_limitations records 'Incomplete overlap between data streams' and the interim/Beta status.
questions.quality_note: One bias is identified and categorised with a BiasTypeEnum value, which is more than free-text mention, but there is no AIO mapping, no fairness analysis and no coverage of the foreseeable selection biases from the curated panel of '100 chromatin modifiers and 100 metabolic enzymes' or the incomplete modality overlap already noted as a limitation.

strengths: Complete, corroborated funding and creator metadata: valid NIH grant numbers with RePORTER detail, six creator groups with affiliations, credit roles, PIs and ORCIDs.
Fully specified access path: public Dataverse releases with per-release DOIs, per-file names, md5 checksums and sizes, an API route for large files, and no approval step.

Governance and sustainability are documented end to end: CC BY-NC-SA license with named copyright holders, a Data Access Committee with contact, LibraData preservation 'supported by committed institutional funds', errata and a release archive.
Interoperability grounded in RO-Crate/FAIRSCAPE packaging with ARK identifiers, EVI provenance graphs, Croissant/Schema.org exports, ontology IRIs on instances and Cellosaurus RRIDs on cell lines.

Disciplined sourcing: referent scoping excludes the U2OS Nature study from composition and funding, and every conflicting figure (release dates, protein counts, institution lists, award end) is recorded with a source_caveats line rather than resolved silently.
weaknesses: No dataset-level doi; id duplicates page (project web site) although the release DOI is used in citation and version_access.
Data payload formats are opaque: every data file is 'ZIP' with contents unstated, and no common identifier scheme for cross-modality or cross-dataset linking is named.
collection_timeframes carries the NIH award period rather than acquisition dates; no top-level version, and per-release version numbers are inconsistent (two releases at '2.1', the newest at '2.0').
Bias and social-impact coverage is thin: one typed bias, no fairness analysis, no future_use_impacts or discouraged_uses.
No cleaning, QC, imputation or missing-data documentation; ethical_reviews entries are contact persons rather than review determinations.
recommendations: Set doi to 10.18130/V3/HIGT4C and use it as id; add a top-level version matching the Dataverse dataset version and a caveat on the per-release numbering scheme.
State the contained file formats per archive (images, mass-spectrometry tables, perturb-seq matrices, sequencing reads) and the gene/protein identifier namespace used across modalities.
Move the award period to the grant entry and either leave collection_timeframes with a declared gap or bound it by release dates; add total_size_bytes from the stated file sizes.
Add selection_bias entries for the curated protein panel and incomplete modality overlap, plus a future_use_impacts entry covering dual-use and commercialisation supervision.
Document QC and missing-data handling for the released input streams, and recast ethical_reviews as a review determination (or explicit no-IRB-required statement) with contacts moved to governance.
